purpose: Development set frozen before the structural rewrite; source-backed expected facts, not exact wording. No held-out or embedding-system claim.

questions.query: Which exact local version do we have, and can I recover its uncommitted changes?
facts: Distinguish the actual inspected local checkpoint and dirty tree from the reconstructed upstream base and historical M11 source.
Name verified recovery coverage and limitations; a base hash or export identity does not prove current commit or backup coverage.

questions.query: Who is allowed to mutate the cells, and can a worker touch a Godot object?
facts: Native World owns authoritative cellular state.
Desktop Godot worker exclusively calls its adapter/value APIs; internal native workers call no Godot APIs; live scene-tree and Rapier objects remain on the allowed Godot thread.
Web has synchronous main-thread ownership.

questions.query: Does enabling browser threads let drawing continue while the simulation tick is still running?
facts: No: Web waits synchronously for each native cellular tick.
Pthreads parallelize native tick work; publication cadence is separate but asynchronous Web simulation/render ownership is unimplemented.
Desktop has an asynchronous Godot worker.

questions.query: What CPU counts does Auto choose in compatibility and threaded Web builds?
facts: Compatibility forces one cellular worker.
Auto chooses 2 for logical thread count below 4, 4 for counts from 4 through 11, and 6 from 12 upward in the threaded profile.
Worker count does not imply concurrent Web presentation ownership.

questions.query: Are body physics, the player, and cellular updates ordered the same on desktop and Web?
facts: No shared exact lockstep is established.
Desktop character update precedes cells in the asynchronous owner; main-thread Rapier exchanges samples/results.
Web applies previous results, steps Rapier, prepares the mask, ticks cells, then moves the character; pending terrain chunks gate Web advancement.

questions.query: What happens to play when a native simulation tick fails?
facts: Failed ticks may advance attempted tick/epoch and mutate cells/events; there is no rollback.
World latches failure and rejects further ticks/gameplay writes/publication; completed tick identity does not advance.
Desktop publishes stopped status retaining its last valid payload; Web pauses/menu-reports and suppresses partial output; Rapier stays main-thread owned.
Explicit reset/clear or validated replacement is required; accepted events are never automatically replayed and invalid replacement retains the fault.

questions.query: Are we using Rapier or Godot physics, which version, and who advances it?
facts: Rapier2D 0.35.2 single precision is the selected backend.
The main Godot thread manually steps Rapier; workers receive values, not live physics objects.
Both Web profiles include Rapier by default; separate dated platform evidence is required.

questions.query: When a crate moves across sand, do we erase its old pixels and put them back?
facts: No: the rectangle proof builds a separate sampled obstacle projection.
Movable overlap cells use bounded ordered ejection; unresolved cells remain and are counted.
General fracture and particle fallback are not Current.

questions.query: What prevents terrain contacts and sand coupling from pushing a body twice?
facts: Rapier owns hard-terrain contacts in the current adapter.
The Rapier path suppresses duplicate cellular Wall correction/support; capped cellular impact, pressure and displacement contributions remain.
Generalized backend-neutral coupling contracts are separate from this rectangle proof.

questions.query: What exactly crosses the rigid body bridge, and how many bodies can it handle?
facts: The prototype packed float32 input/result strides are 11 and 9, with at most 64 accepted bodies after ACT-004; every admitted field is finite and body IDs are exact integers 1 through 64.
Values carry body/sample identity and numeric rectangle state/results; no Node, RID or live direct state crosses.
This is a prototype layout, not the approved generalized native ABI.

questions.query: If importing a level gives the exact same save string, will the next tick replay exactly too?
facts: No: CYSD1 reconstructs a finite level; identical re-export proves saved payload restoration only.
Tick/epoch, scheduler activity, complete configuration, pending commands and Rapier internal solver state are omitted.
A full durable exact-replay checkpoint and general strict mode remain Planned.

questions.query: What is inside a CYSD1 file, and can it save an arbitrary sparse world?
facts: Current encoding is fixed at 1024 by 1024 with five native bytes per cell: material, state_a, state_b and LE16 temperature.
A 56-byte header, bounded JSON metadata, DEFLATE payload, SHA-256 integrity and Base64 text form the container.
General sparse-world persistence is Planned.

questions.query: Can saving the level alter anything, and does a bad import damage the running world?
facts: Export requires exclusive safe-boundary ownership and clears the transient obstacle projection while copying stored-cell temperatures.
Coupling must rebuild before the next cellular tick.
Import validates and constructs a fresh World before swapping, preserving the old world on invalid input.

questions.query: Do matching state hashes prove complete deterministic replay, including bodies and future inputs?
facts: No: exact comparisons cover specified repeated or worker-parity cellular fixtures.
state_hash includes tick/epoch, selected config, cell/activity state and queued explosions but omits relevant external/controller/body state and some settings.
content_hash excludes scheduling/tick details and is the rest-stability check; neither is complete replay persistence.

questions.query: Can the renderer read live cells or reuse a patch buffer before upload finishes?
facts: No: published patches have immutable snapshot or lease-owned lifetime, and the Godot adapter copies values.
Consumer validates metadata and bytes before Image construction/blit; acknowledgement follows successful consumption.
Malformed/rejected patches request a full refresh rather than reading mutable World storage.

questions.query: If all snapshot slots are still in use or a patch is too large, is dirty data lost?
facts: No: native publish returns Backpressure or CapacityExceeded and preserves unacknowledged dirty state.
Required patch/byte counts and high-water observations are explicit; no mutable fallback or hidden growth.
Published slots stay immutable until the final lease releases.

questions.query: Dirty rectangles are small, so are we uploading only those pixels to the GPU?
facts: Current RG8 CPU patches are sparse, but ImageTexture.update uploads the whole 1024-square two-byte texture (2,097,152 bytes).
True GPU subregion upload is not implemented; patch work and GPU upload cost must be measured separately.

questions.query: Are simulation tiles double buffered, and how are writes into a neighboring tile made safe?
facts: Current default is phased in-place: 64-square scheduling cores, four parity phases, bounded radius-two ownership.
Workers write exclusively within their phase domains and effects merge deterministically.
A buffered backend enum/name does not mean the planned buffered algorithm or transfer sort tuple exists.

questions.query: Is the world really limited to 1024 pixels or twice the camera size?
facts: Native World uses sparse chunks with signed coordinates and explicit capacities; 1024-square is the current demo/save adapter scope.
The interest region and storage capacity differ; the 2x validation target is not a permanent world-size limit.
General safe live capacity reconfiguration and sparse persistence remain Planned.

questions.query: What happens if I enqueue too many explosions or run out of reserved simulation space?
facts: Explosion enqueue rejects invalid/full input explicitly; effects are tick-boundary bounded work.

Capacity behavior is API-specific and must be reported. Avoiding hot tick allocation is an Approved target and Current only for preallocated fixture scope; lazy coordinator preparation may allocate chunks or temperature storage.
WorldConfig capacity defaults are not universal runtime adapter defaults; live resize is not already implemented.

questions.query: Does native Water move twenty-four cells per update, and what does viscosity mean?
facts: The 24-cell travel rule belongs to the discrete GDScript fallback, not native Water.
Native Water stores 1-255 mass in state_a and performs conserved pairwise gravity/diagonal/lateral transfers.
Viscosity scales native lateral transfer rate independently of yield and adhesion; Water viscosity is zero.

questions.query: How do calm water emission and the adhesion toggle differ?
facts: Calm/coherent emission uses an explicit command flag and a 12-tick state_b delay on lateral spread, not a new material.
The native adhesion toggle independently retains supported Water film at or below 48/255 when enabled.
Viscosity, yield and adhesion are distinct; fallback rules differ.

questions.query: How should I tell whether a shimmering pool is a fluid bug or just its shader?
facts: Inspect content changes/mass/dirty observations; state_hash advances with ticks and is not a stable-rest oracle.
Stable coordinate/mass dithering is presentation-only and must not wake or mutate cells.
Settling/conservation evidence applies to bounded named fixtures, not arbitrary mixtures.

questions.query: Can we approximate interactions to keep frame times stable, and is strict mode available now?
facts: Bounded explicit approximation is Approved for runtime secondary work, preserving ownership, collision/occupancy and conservation constraints.
Exact fixture validation remains required.
A general selectable strict runtime mode and complete exact replay are Planned, not Current; local 2x2 occupancy coarsening is Rejected.

questions.query: Can we move authoritative materials to GPU compute, or author their rules in arbitrary JavaScript?
facts: Authoritative local occupancy remains native CPU; GPU compute is Deferred pending ownership/readback/replay evidence.
An item-authored bounded native program is Planned; arbitrary per-cell JavaScript is Rejected.
Presentation-only GPU effects do not confer authority.

questions.query: Do SimulationCore and GameplayBridge already exist as reusable implementation modules?
facts: These are target semantic module names, not an assertion of implemented classes/APIs.
Current native World, C ABI, GDExtension, GDScript worker and rectangle proof are concrete surfaces.
Generalized interfaces need design review; map Approved/Planned names to actual source.

questions.query: What smoke, pressure and heat simulation actually runs today?
facts: Current native Smoke has bounded lifetime/crowd collapse and cannot burn or host Fire.
Current temperature storage/material reactions are not a complete generalized heat/pressure field solver.
Future fields and visual tuning must remain separately marked Planned or Deferred.

questions.query: Which exact tools should I build with, and can I share the native and Web bindings checkout?
facts: Use pinned Godot 4.7 official 5b4e0cb0f, godot-cpp 101ae38034304346a46ea9ea84ae156d3e860496 and Emscripten 4.0.20; local Windows LLVM-MinGW and SCons pins are explicit.
Keep native and Web generated bindings separate.
Use local dev wrappers and distinguish local override from historical release provenance.

questions.query: If an export checksum passes or build-info names the base commit, is the browser build proven current?
facts: No: export-only structural validation/checksums do not prove fresh source-to-artifact build or browser execution.
source_commit records a snapshot base, not full local changes; retain current source and binary identities with dated evidence.
HTTP checks, headless fixtures, actual browser runtime and visual inspection are different validation scopes.

questions.query: Do the old sanitizer results and current Windows fixtures prove Linux, Firefox and Safari work?
facts: No: M11 sanitizer/results are historical with their recorded revision/platform scope; current Windows tests do not prove other platforms.

Dated Chromium compatibility/threaded evidence is separate. Current Linux native, headless and rendered-fixture results have their own source/runtime records, including the MAT-002 review; old sanitizer or Windows results do not establish them. Firefox/Safari execution remains unestablished by these records.
LFS pointer files are not usable runtime binaries and historical totals must not be relabelled as fresh passes.

questions.query: Why is the old consistency check red, and should I update its hashes to make the release pass?
facts: The old check compares current files to M11; strict comparison still reports drift, including unresolved payload pointers. Preserve previous failures.
M11 integrity now checks all 28 original source hashes against the audited Git revision and 18 retained records. Never rewrite historical hashes.
Current checks independently validate documentation, dependency versions and source-bound runtime/LFS identity; identity does not prove execution.
Web CI/toolchain/template/export provenance contradictions remain separate issue #3 obligations.

questions.query: After changing physics ownership, which documentation and evidence must I update before a checkpoint?
facts: Map affected canonical contracts, ownership/lifetimes, invariants, configuration, ADR, roadmap, build/test guide and retrieval routes.
Record actual source/checkpoint identity and scoped validation; search aliases and reverse links for stale duplicate claims.
Keep historical records intact and run structural/link/retrieval checks plus relevant behavioral checks.
